newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma to sell natgas to Thailand from Yetagun.
newsitem.headline: Burma to sell natgas to Thailand from Yetagun.

text.p: Burma will sell 200 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of natural gas to Thailand from Yetagun, its second offshore natural gas field in the Andaman Sea, official newspapers reported on Monday.
"Gas from the Yetagun natural gas project will be sold to Thailand at 200 million cubic feet per day beginning 1999," the state run newspapers said.
"A two inch diametre pipe will be laid for 40 miles inland and 130 miles offshore," they said.
The Yetagun gas project base camp was formally opened in Kanbauk Village, about 400 miles (640 km) southeast of Rangoon, on Sunday.

The Yetagun gas field was discovered by Texaco in Blocks M-12/M-13 in Tanintharyi Shelf. The field has the potential of producing 7,000 barrels of condensate and 200 mmcfd of natural gas from good to excellent quality sandstone reservoirs, official records show.
The Yetagun field is Burma's second offshore field supplying natural gas to Thailand.
Burma is already exploiting gas from the Yadana field in the Bay of Mattama under a 30-year contract beween the Ministry of Energy and the Petroleum Authority of Thailand.
Sales will begin at 525 mmcfd of natural gas in July 1998.
The Yadana field has potential deposits of 6.7 trillion cubic feet of natural gas and 5.7 trillion cubic feet of commercial deposits, official statistics show.
